Python: loading data

Source: vignettes/articles/python-data.Rmd
python-data.Rmd

Plots and the species records observed in them, from CSV files or data frames, into a RESOLVE engine dataset: the roles that name the columns, the targets, the loader settings, the dataset and its schema, the vocabularies that code species, genera and families as integers, and the species graph.

All of the Python reference

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")

# The RESOLVE engine library, downloaded once
library(resolveR)
resolve.install_backend()
pip install resolve-core

The examples on this page run in order on the survey that ships with the R package: 150 plots in the Alps, with one table of plots and one of the species recorded on them.

RoleMapping 

RoleMapping()

Names the columns of the two tables by the part they play in a dataset. A role is such a part: the plot identifier, the species name, the abundance, the taxonomy, the coordinates and the plot-level covariates. Every attribute starts unset; set the ones your tables carry.

import pandas as pd
import resolve_core as rc

data = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcol33/resolve/master/r/inst/extdata/"
plots = pd.read_csv(data + "plots.csv")
species = pd.read_csv(data + "species.csv")

roles = rc.RoleMapping()
roles.plot_id = "plot_id"
roles.species_id = "species"
roles.abundance = "cover"
roles.genus = "genus"
roles.family = "family"
roles.latitude = "lat"
roles.longitude = "lon"
roles.has_coordinates()

Attributes:

  • plot_id (str): the plot identifier, a column of both tables. Required.
  • species_id (str): the species name in the species table. Required.
  • abundance (str or None): the abundance or cover column of the species table.
  • genus, family (str or None): the genus and family columns of the species table.
  • latitude, longitude (str or None): the coordinate columns of the plot table, in degrees.
  • covariates (list[str]): numeric plot-table columns the model reads, standardised on the fitting plots.
  • categoricals (list[str]): text plot-table columns, each coded as integers when the data is loaded. A column is a covariate or a categorical, never both.
  • targets (list[str]): a list of column names the loaders do not read; they take the targets from the TargetSpec list.

Methods: has_coordinates() is true when both coordinate columns are set, has_taxonomy() when the genus or the family is, has_abundance() and has_categoricals() when those are.

TargetSpec 

TargetSpec.regression(column, transform=TransformType.None_)
TargetSpec.classification(column, num_classes)
TargetSpec.classification_with_mapping(column, mapping)

One target, a plot-table column the model learns to impute, and how its values are read. A regression target is a number; a classification target is a class label. classification codes the labels in alphabetical order; classification_with_mapping takes the code of every label from mapping. num_classes of 0 reads the class count off the data.

targets = [rc.TargetSpec.regression("elevation"),
           rc.TargetSpec.classification("habitat", 4)]

habitat = rc.TargetSpec.classification_with_mapping(
    "habitat", {"alpine": 0, "forest": 1, "grassland": 2, "wetland": 3})

elevation = rc.TargetSpec.regression("elevation")
elevation.missing = rc.TargetMissingPolicy.Mask
elevation.weight = 2.0

Attributes:

  • column_name (str): the column read from the plot table.
  • target_name (str): the name the target is reported under, the column name by default.
  • task (TaskType): regression or classification.
  • transform (TransformType): Log1p stores log(1 + y) and trains on it; imputed values and metrics come back in the original units.
  • num_classes (int): the class count of a classification target.
  • class_mapping (dict[str, int]): the label-to-code map; empty when the codes are fitted alphabetically.
  • weight (float, default 1.0): the target’s weight in the loss summed over targets.
  • missing (TargetMissingPolicy, default Drop): what happens to a plot with no value for this target.

TaskType

The kind of a target: Regression or Classification.

TransformType

The transform a regression target is stored under: None_ (the values as recorded) or Log1p (log(1 + y)).

TargetMissingPolicy

What a plot with no value for a target does. Under Drop, the default, the plot leaves the dataset. Under Mask the plot stays and holds -1 (classification) or NaN (regression) for this target: it trains and is scored on its other targets, and this target’s loss, scaler, metrics and baselines read only the plots labelled for it. A plot labelled for no target is left out under either policy.

DatasetConfig 

DatasetConfig()

How the species recorded on a plot become model input. The encoding is the form a plot’s species set takes as input: hashed into a fixed-width vector (Hash), a fixed number of ranked species slots (Embed), a sparse vector over the species vocabulary (Sparse), or every species weighted and pooled (RankPool) or read as a sequence by attention layers (Transformer). Encoding the species set compares them.

config = rc.DatasetConfig()
config.species_encoding = rc.SpeciesEncodingMode.Embed
config.top_k_species = 10

Attributes:

  • species_encoding (SpeciesEncodingMode, default Hash): the encoding.
  • hash_dim (int, default 32): the width of the hashed vector.
  • top_k (int, default 3): the species per plot the hash encoding keeps, and the number of genus and family slots of the hash, sparse and embed encodings.
  • top_k_species (int, default 10): the species slots of the embed encoding.
  • selection (SelectionMode, default Top): which species of a plot survive its budget, ranked by recorded abundance, ties by name.
  • species_budget (int, default 0): the species per plot kept under RankPool, Transformer and Sparse, taken from the end of the ranking selection names; 0 keeps every species.
  • representation (RepresentationMode, default Abundance): the value each species carries into every encoding, its abundance or 1.0. The selection still ranks by recorded abundance.
  • normalization (NormalizationMode, default Raw): how the hash weights of a plot’s selected species are rescaled.
  • aggregation (AggregationMode, default Abundance): how the genus and family slots rank a plot’s taxa, and how RankPool and Transformer weight each species’ genus and family.
  • pool_weighting (PoolWeighting, default Log1p): the weight each species pools with under RankPool and Transformer.
  • pool_species_cap (int, default 0): the most species per plot RankPool and Transformer read. 0 is no cap; a positive number caps at that many; -x caps at the (100 - x)th percentile of the plots’ species counts (-1 the 99th). A longer plot keeps its most abundant species.
  • track_unknown_fraction (bool, default True): add an input column with each plot’s share of abundance from species outside the vocabulary.
  • track_unknown_count (bool, default False): add an input column with each plot’s number of such species.
  • use_taxonomy (bool, default True): read the genus and family when the roles name them.
  • missing_values (MissingValuePolicy, default Indicate): how a blank covariate or coordinate cell enters the model.
  • zero_abundance_as (float, default 0.0): the abundance a record of exactly 0 is read at. Archives that write a presence without a cover estimate as 0 read as absent under log1p weighting; 1.0 reads them at the weight of a record with no cover.
  • use_cuda_hash (bool, default False): compute the hash encoding on the GPU for each batch instead of storing it at load.

A species recorded several times on one plot, such as once per vegetation layer, is one entry of that plot: its abundances are summed and it carries the alphabetically first genus and family of its records. Every encoding, the vocabulary and the unknown-species columns read these entries.

SpeciesEncodingMode

The encoding of a plot’s species set: Hash, Embed, Sparse, RankPool or Transformer.

SelectionMode

Which species of a plot fill its budget, ranked by abundance: Top (the most abundant), Bottom (the least abundant), TopBottom (the budget from each end) or All (every species). The embed encoding refuses All, because its slots are fixed in number.

RepresentationMode

The value a species carries into the encoding: Abundance (its recorded abundance) or PresenceAbsence (1.0).

NormalizationMode

How the hash weights of a plot’s selected species are rescaled: Raw (unchanged), Norm (divided by their sum) or Log1p.

AggregationMode

How taxa are ranked and weighted. Under Abundance a genus or family slot ranks taxa by the summed value of their species, and RankPool and Transformer weight each species’ genus and family with the species weight. Under Count the slots rank taxa by how many of the plot’s species they hold, and every species weighs one.

PoolWeighting

The weight a species pools with under RankPool and Transformer: Binary (1), Abundance, Log1p (log(1 + abundance)), Norm (the abundance over the plot’s total) or Rank (a weight falling with the species’ abundance rank).

MissingValuePolicy

How a blank covariate or coordinate cell enters the model. Under Indicate, the default, the model reads the mean of the fitting plots in its place and a 0/1 column marks it (one per covariate, one for the coordinate pair). Under Zero the cell reads as 0.0 with no mark, so a recorded 0 and a missing value are one input. The dataset keeps a missing cell as NaN in coordinates and covariates under either policy.

effective_selection() 

effective_selection(config)

The species selection a dataset loaded under config applies. The hash and embed encodings always select, because their widths are per-plot budgets (top_k, top_k_species). RankPool, Transformer and Sparse select only when species_budget gives them a budget, and report All otherwise. A dataset records this value on its schema.

rc.effective_selection(config)

ResolveDataset

The loaded and encoded plots. A dataset is built by one of the static loaders below; it has no public constructor.

from_pandas() 

ResolveDataset.from_pandas(header, species=None, roles=None, targets=None,
                           config=None, schema_source=None, vocabs=None)

A dataset from pandas data frames. header is the plot table and species the species table, one row per record. With species a path to a CSV file, the plot table stays in memory and the species table is read from the file. With species=None, header is a single long table holding both, as from_species_csv reads it. schema_source, a dataset, reuses its vocabularies and class codes; vocabs, an ExternalVocabs (a predictor’s external_vocabs, or a fine-tuning parent’s vocabs()), codes the plots in a trained model’s namespace. Both need the two tables as data frames, and only one of them is given. from_dataframe is the same function.

The cells are written as text the way DataFrame.to_csv writes them, a missing value as the empty string, so the dataset equals the one from_csv loads from the CSV files the frames would write.

dataset = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets, config)
dataset.n_plots
dataset.species_ids.shape

from_csv() 

ResolveDataset.from_csv(header_path, species_path, roles, targets,
                        config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_species_csv(species_path, roles, targets,
                                config=DatasetConfig())

A dataset from a plot CSV file and a species CSV file, or from one long species file that also holds the plot columns. from_species_csv reads a plot’s coordinates and targets from its first record and carries no covariates or categoricals.

import os
import tempfile

folder = tempfile.mkdtemp()
plots.to_csv(os.path.join(folder, "plots.csv"), index=False)
species.to_csv(os.path.join(folder, "species.csv"), index=False)
from_files = rc.ResolveDataset.from_csv(
    os.path.join(folder, "plots.csv"), os.path.join(folder, "species.csv"),
    roles, targets, config)

Loaders that reuse vocabularies 

ResolveDataset.from_csv_with_schema(header_path, species_path, roles, targets,
                                    schema_source, config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_csv_with_vocabs(header_path, species_path, roles, targets,
                                    vocabs, config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_species_csv_with_schema(species_path, roles, targets,
                                            schema, config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_species_csv_with_vocabs(species_path, roles, targets,
                                            vocabs, config=DatasetConfig())

A vocabulary maps each species, genus or family name to the integer code a model reads. These loaders code new plots with the vocabularies of an earlier dataset or a trained checkpoint, so each code means what it meant in training. schema_source is a ResolveDataset or a ResolveSchema; a schema lets a checkpoint stand in for training files that no longer exist. vocabs is an ExternalVocabs, the complete form, because the categorical codes live on the Predictor and not on the schema. A species the vocabulary does not hold is unknown, and counts toward the unknown-species columns.

reloaded = rc.ResolveDataset.from_csv_with_schema(
    os.path.join(folder, "plots.csv"), os.path.join(folder, "species.csv"),
    roles, targets, dataset.schema, config)

Loaders from string columns 

ResolveDataset.from_columns(header_names, header_columns, species_names,
                            species_columns, roles, targets, config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_columns_header(header_names, header_columns, species_path,
                                   roles, targets, config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_columns_with_schema(header_names, header_columns, species_names,
                                        species_columns, roles, targets,
                                        schema_source, config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_columns_with_vocabs(header_names, header_columns, species_names,
                                        species_columns, roles, targets, vocabs,
                                        config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_species_columns(species_names, species_columns, roles, targets,
                                    config=DatasetConfig())
ResolveDataset.from_species_columns_with_vocabs(species_names, species_columns,
                                                roles, targets, vocabs,
                                                config=DatasetConfig())

The in-memory forms of the CSV loaders. A table is a list of column names and a list of columns, each a list of strings with the empty string for a missing cell. from_pandas builds these from data frames; call them directly for tables held in another form, or to reuse an ExternalVocabs on data in memory.

names = list(plots.columns)
columns = [plots[c].astype(str).tolist() for c in names]
species_names = list(species.columns)
species_columns = [species[c].astype(str).tolist() for c in species_names]
from_strings = rc.ResolveDataset.from_columns_with_vocabs(
    names, columns, species_names, species_columns, roles, targets,
    dataset.external_vocabs(), config)

Attributes

  • schema (ResolveSchema): the structure of the dataset, which a model is built from and a checkpoint carries.
  • config (DatasetConfig): the settings the loader ran with.
  • n_plots (int): the plots after the target-driven drops.
  • plot_ids (list[str]): the plot identifiers, in row order.
  • species_vocab (list[str]): the species vocabulary in code order; code 0 is "<UNK>", the unknown species.
  • taxonomy_vocab (TaxonomyVocab) and categorical_vocab (CategoricalVocab): the fitted genus, family and categorical codes.
  • targets (dict[str, Tensor]): the target values, in the space the loader stored them.

The model inputs are torch tensors, or None where the encoding does not produce them:

  • coordinates ((n_plots, 2)) and covariates ((n_plots, n_covariates)), missing cells NaN; categorical_ids ((n_plots, n_categoricals)).
  • hash_embedding ((n_plots, hash_dim)): the hash encoding, without use_cuda_hash.
  • species_ids: the species codes of the embed slots ((n_plots, top_k_species)) or of every pooled species ((n_plots, max_species)).
  • species_vector ((n_plots, n_species_vocab)): the sparse encoding, a torch sparse CSR tensor. crow_indices() delimits the plots, col_indices() holds each plot’s species codes in increasing order and values() their values; to_dense() gives the matrix.
  • genus_ids, family_ids ((n_plots, n_taxonomy_slots)): the genus and family slots of the hash, sparse and embed encodings.
  • pool_genus_ids, pool_family_ids, pool_weights, pool_mask ((n_plots, max_species)) and pool_has_cover ((n_plots,)): the pooled species of RankPool and Transformer.
  • unknown_fraction, unknown_count ((n_plots,)): the unknown-species columns.
  • species_genus_ids, species_family_ids ((n_species_vocab,)): the genus and family code of each species of the vocabulary, 0 where its records name none.
  • raw_species_ids, raw_weights, plot_offsets: under use_cuda_hash, each plot’s selected species in flat compressed form: plot p holds entries plot_offsets[p] to plot_offsets[p + 1].

The unknown-species columns are measured against the vocabulary the dataset is coded with, over each plot’s whole species list. A training load fits that vocabulary on its own records, so they read 0 there; they carry information on the loaders that reuse a vocabulary.

Methods

  • plot_indices(ids): the position of each plot identifier in plot_ids, in the order given, the held-out fold Trainer.prepare_data takes. Raises ValueError for an identifier the dataset does not hold.
  • continuous_block(include_hash): the unstandardised continuous block, the numeric input columns side by side: coordinates, covariates, their missingness columns, the unknown-species columns and, with include_hash, the hash encoding. This is the continuous argument of ResolveModel.forward.
  • external_vocabs(): an ExternalVocabs holding every vocabulary the dataset fitted.
  • has_pool_data(): true under RankPool and Transformer. has_raw_species_data(): true under use_cuda_hash.
dataset.plot_indices(["A001", "A003"])
dataset.continuous_block(False).shape

ResolveSchema

The structure of a loaded dataset: the input widths, the targets and the vocabularies. A model is sized from it and a checkpoint carries it.

schema = dataset.schema
schema.n_species_vocab
[t.name for t in schema.targets]

Attributes:

  • n_plots (int): the plots after the target-driven drops.
  • n_species (int): the distinct species. n_species_vocab (int): the vocabulary size, the unknown slot included.
  • n_genera, n_families (int): the taxonomy vocabulary sizes, the unknown slot included.
  • covariate_names, categorical_names (list[str]): the plot-level columns, in input order.
  • categorical_vocab_sizes (list[int]) and categorical_embed_dim (int): the code count of each categorical column and its embedding width.
  • targets (list[TargetConfig]): one per target.
  • has_coordinates, has_abundance, has_taxonomy (bool): what the data carried.
  • species_vocab, genus_vocab, family_vocab (list[str]): the vocabularies in code order, "<UNK>" first.
  • dataset_config (DatasetConfig): the loader settings the dataset was coded with. selection is the selection applied (effective_selection), and pool_species_cap the width a pooled load truncated to.
  • unrecorded_dataset_settings (list[str]): the DatasetConfig fields a checkpoint written before they existed does not carry; each reads as the RESOLVE engine’s behaviour before the setting existed. Empty for a dataset’s own schema.

Methods: has_categoricals(), n_categoricals(), has_species_vocab() and has_taxonomy_vocab() (false for a checkpoint written before vocabularies travelled with it), and missing_flag_width(), the number of missingness columns the continuous block holds.

TargetConfig

One entry of ResolveSchema.targets: a target as the dataset loaded it.

Attributes:

  • name (str), task (TaskType), transform (TransformType), weight (float): as on the TargetSpec.
  • num_classes (int): the class count of a classification target.
  • class_names (list[str]): the labels in code order; empty for a regression target.
  • class_weights (list[float]): per-class weights of the cross-entropy; empty for an unweighted target.
  • missing (TargetMissingPolicy): the policy the target was loaded and trained under.

ExternalVocabs

Every vocabulary a dataset fitted, in the form the *_with_vocabs loaders take. Predictor.external_vocabs returns the complete set of a checkpoint, the categorical codes included; ResolveDataset.external_vocabs() that of a dataset.

vocabs = dataset.external_vocabs()
len(vocabs.species_vocab)

Attributes:

  • species_vocab (list[str]): the species names in code order.
  • taxonomy (TaxonomyVocab) and categorical (CategoricalVocab): the genus, family and categorical codes.
  • targets (list[TargetConfig]): the targets, with their class codes.
  • pool_species_cap (int): the pooled width the source’s records were truncated to, or 0. A dataset coded with these vocabularies is truncated to it in place of its own pool_species_cap.

external_vocabs_from_schema() 

external_vocabs_from_schema(schema)

The vocabularies a schema carries, as an ExternalVocabs. The categorical codes are not on the schema: take them from Predictor.categorical_vocab, or use Predictor.external_vocabs, which includes them.

from_schema = rc.external_vocabs_from_schema(dataset.schema)

EncodingVocab

The species vocabulary and the taxonomy vocabulary one encoding codes a plot with: species (SpeciesVocab) and taxonomy (TaxonomyVocab). has_taxonomy() is true when the taxonomy was fitted. The standalone encoders below hold one, as vocab, and take one with set_vocab(vocab).

SpeciesVocab 

SpeciesVocab.from_records(records, min_count=1)
SpeciesVocab.from_ordered(names)

The species vocabulary: each name to an integer code, 0 for an unknown species. from_records fits it on SpeciesRecords: the species recorded in at least min_count plots, coded 1 to K by descending plot count, ties by name. from_ordered rebuilds one fitted elsewhere from its names in code order, names[0] being "<UNK>".

Members: encode(name) (0 for a name it does not hold), names, species_to_id, size() (the unknown slot included) and empty().

TaxonomyVocab

The genus and family vocabularies, each name to an integer code, 0 for unknown. fit(records) fits both on SpeciesRecords; encode_genus(name), encode_family(name), n_genera() and n_families() read them. save(archive, prefix) and load(archive, prefix) take libtorch’s C++ serialization archives, which Python cannot construct; a checkpoint carries the taxonomy on its schema.

CategoricalVocab

The integer codes of each categorical column: 1 to K for the values seen, 0 for an unknown or missing value.

Members: fit_column(column_name, raw_values), encode(column_name, raw_value), vocab_size(column_name) (the unknown slot included), has_column(column_name), column_map(column_name) (dict[str, int]), column_names and vocab_sizes.

soil = rc.CategoricalVocab()
soil.fit_column("soil", ["acid", "base", "acid"])
soil.column_map("soil")

SpeciesRecord 

SpeciesRecord()

One species recorded on one plot, the input of the standalone encoders and vocabularies: plot_id, species_id, genus, family (str) and abundance (float).

records = []
for row in species.itertuples():
    record = rc.SpeciesRecord()
    record.plot_id = row.plot_id
    record.species_id = row.species
    record.genus = row.genus
    record.family = row.family
    record.abundance = float(row.cover)
    records.append(record)

vocab = rc.SpeciesVocab.from_records(records)
vocab.encode("Carex curvula")

EmbeddingEncoder 

EmbeddingEncoder(top_k_species=10, top_k_taxonomy=3,
                 selection=SelectionMode.Top,
                 aggregation=AggregationMode.Abundance)

The embed encoding on its own, outside a dataset: top_k_species ranked species slots and top_k_taxonomy genus and family slots per plot. selection fills the species slots; All is refused. aggregation ranks the taxonomy slots.

Methods: fit(records) fits the vocabularies, transform(records, plot_ids, representation=RepresentationMode.Abundance) codes the plots in the order of plot_ids and returns an EmbeddingEncodedData. is_fitted(), n_species_vocab(), n_genera(), n_families(), vocab, species_vocab, taxonomy_vocab and set_vocab(vocab) read or replace the vocabularies.

embed = rc.EmbeddingEncoder(top_k_species=5)
embed.fit(records)
slots = embed.transform(records, ["A001", "A002"])
slots.species_ids.shape

EmbeddingEncodedData

What EmbeddingEncoder.transform returns: species_ids ((n_plots, top_k_species)), genus_ids and family_ids ((n_plots, top_k_taxonomy)), all int64.

RankPoolEncoder 

RankPoolEncoder(weighting=PoolWeighting.Log1p, min_frequency=1,
                selection=SelectionMode.All, species_budget=0)

The rank-pool encoding on its own: every species of a plot with its weight, padded to the widest plot. selection and species_budget narrow each plot first, as in DatasetConfig; the defaults keep every species.

Methods: fit(records); transform(records, plot_ids, species_cap=0, has_abundance_column=False, representation=RepresentationMode.Abundance) returns a RankPoolEncodedData. species_cap reads as DatasetConfig.pool_species_cap. has_abundance_column sets has_cover to 1 for every plot. The vocabulary members are those of EmbeddingEncoder.

pool = rc.RankPoolEncoder()
pool.fit(records)
pooled = pool.transform(records, ["A001", "A002"], has_abundance_column=True)
pooled.weights

RankPoolEncodedData

What RankPoolEncoder.transform returns, each (n_plots, max_species): species_ids, genus_ids, family_ids (int64), weights (float), mask (bool, true at a species), and has_cover ((n_plots,), 1 where the abundance was recorded).

build_species_graph() 

build_species_graph(dataset, config)

The graph over the species vocabulary a heterogeneous graph neural network passes messages on, from a dataset and a HeterogeneousGNNConfig. Species sharing a genus or a family are joined by an edge when use_taxonomic_edges is set. With use_cooccurrence_edges, a species is joined to the k_cooccurrence species it shares most plots with, among those sharing at least one plot and at least cooccurrence_threshold of all plots, ties to the lower code; the counts come from species_vector, so these edges need the sparse encoding. Trainer.prepare_data builds the graph itself and the checkpoint carries it, so call this to inspect the graph or to build a variant for ResolveModel.set_species_graph.

sparse = rc.DatasetConfig()
sparse.species_encoding = rc.SpeciesEncodingMode.Sparse
sparse_data = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets, sparse)
graph = rc.build_species_graph(sparse_data, rc.ModelConfig().heterogeneous_gnn)
graph.n_edges

SpeciesGraph

What build_species_graph returns: edge_index ((2, n_edges), int64 species codes), edge_type ((n_edges,), the SpeciesEdgeType value of each edge), n_edges and n_species.

SpeciesEdgeType

The kind of a species-graph edge, with its code in edge_type: SameGenus (0), SameFamily (1) and CoOccurrence (2).
